audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Joshua / Yehoshua circumcision, Passover, manna cessation, and commander encounter narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for kings' fear, second circumcision, wilderness-generation explanation, Gilgal naming, Passover, produce of land, manna cessation, and commander of YHWH's host.

verses.restored: It was, when all kings of Amorite who were across Jordan toward sea and all kings of Canaanite who were by sea heard that YHWH dried waters of Jordan before children of Israel until we crossed, that their heart melted and there was no spirit in them anymore because of children of Israel.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when all the kings of the Amorites, which were on the side of Jordan westward, and all the kings of the Canaanites, which were by the sea, heard that the LORD had dried up the waters of Jordan from before the children of Israel, until we were passed over, that their heart melted, neither was there spirit in them any more, because of the children of Israel.

modern.text: Now when all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the coast heard how the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over, their hearts melted and their spirits failed for fear of the Israelites.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י כִשְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֡י אֲשֶׁר֩ בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן יָ֗מָּה וְכָל מַלְכֵ֤י הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַיָּ֔ם אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר הוֹבִ֨ישׁ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת מֵ֧י הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן מִפְּנֵ֥י בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַד עברנו וַיִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבָ֗ם וְלֹא הָ֨יָה בָ֥ם עוֹד֙ ר֔וּחַ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: At that time YHWH said to Joshua, Make for yourself knives of flint and circumcise again children of Israel a second time.

familiar.text: At that time the LORD said unto Joshua, Make thee sharp knives, and circumcise again the children of Israel the second time.

modern.text: At that time the LORD said to Joshua, “Make flint knives and circumcise the sons of Israel once again. ”

original.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ עֲשֵׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ חַֽרְב֣וֹת צֻרִ֑ים וְשׁ֛וּב מֹ֥ל אֶת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שֵׁנִֽית

verses.restored: Joshua made for himself knives of flint and circumcised children of Israel at Gibeath-haaraloth/Hill of Foreskins.

familiar.text: And Joshua made him sharp knives, and circumcised the children of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.

modern.text: So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the sons of Israel at Gibeath-haaraloth.

original.text: וַיַּעַשׂ ל֥וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ חַֽרְב֣וֹת צֻרִ֑ים וַיָּ֨מָל֙ אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל גִּבְעַ֖ת הָעֲרָלֽוֹת

verses.restored: This is reason Joshua circumcised them: all people who came out from Egypt, males, all men of war, died in wilderness on way after they came out from Egypt.

familiar.text: And this is the cause why Joshua did circumcise: All the people that came out of Egypt, that were males, even all the men of war, died in the wilderness by the way, after they came out of Egypt.

modern.text: Now this is why Joshua circumcised them: All those who came out of Egypt—all the men of war—had died on the journey in the wilderness after they had left Egypt.

original.text: וְזֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר מָ֣ל יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כָּל הָעָ֣ם הַיֹּצֵא֩ מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם הַזְּכָרִ֜ים כֹּ֣ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה מֵ֤תוּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: For all people who came out were circumcised, but all people born in wilderness on way after coming out from Egypt they had not circumcised.

familiar.text: Now all the people that came out were circumcised: but all the people that were born in the wilderness by the way as they came forth out of Egypt, them they had not circumcised.

modern.text: Though all who had come out were circumcised, none of those born in the wilderness on the journey from Egypt had been circumcised.

original.text: כִּֽי מֻלִ֣ים הָי֔וּ כָּל הָעָ֖ם הַיֹּֽצְאִ֑ים וְכָל הָ֠עָם הַיִּלֹּדִ֨ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר בַּדֶּ֛רֶךְ בְּצֵאתָ֥ם מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם לֹא מָֽלוּ

verses.restored: For forty years children of Israel walked in wilderness until all nation, men of war who came out from Egypt, came to an end because they did not listen to voice of YHWH; YHWH swore to them not to let them see land YHWH swore to their fathers to give us, land flowing with milk and honey.

familiar.text: For the children of Israel walked forty years in the wilderness, till all the people that were men of war, which came out of Egypt, were consumed, because they obeyed not the voice of the LORD: unto whom the LORD sware that he would not shew them the land, which the LORD sware unto their fathers that he would give us, a land that floweth with milk and honey.

modern.text: For the Israelites had wandered in the wilderness forty years, until all the nation’s men of war who had come out of Egypt had died, since they did not obey the LORD. So the LORD vowed never to let them see the land He had sworn to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

original.text: כִּ֣י אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה הָלְכ֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ בַּמִּדְבָּר֒ עַד תֹּ֨ם כָּל הַגּ֜וֹי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הַיֹּצְאִ֣ים מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֞י הַרְאוֹתָ֣ם אֶת הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨ע יְהוָ֤ה לַֽאֲבוֹתָם֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔נוּ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ

verses.restored: Their sons he raised in their place; them Joshua circumcised, for they were uncircumcised because they had not circumcised them on way.

familiar.text: And their children, whom he raised up in their stead, them Joshua circumcised: for they were uncircumcised, because they had not circumcised them by the way.

modern.text: And Joshua raised up their sons in their place, and these were the ones he circumcised. Until this time they were still uncircumcised, since they had not been circumcised along the way.

original.text: וְאֶת בְּנֵיהֶם֙ הֵקִ֣ים תַּחְתָּ֔ם אֹתָ֖ם מָ֣ל יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כִּי עֲרֵלִ֣ים הָי֔וּ כִּ֛י לֹא מָ֥לוּ אוֹתָ֖ם בַּדָּֽרֶךְ

verses.restored: It was, when all nation finished being circumcised, they remained in their place in camp until they recovered.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when they had done circumcising all the people, that they abode in their places in the camp, till they were whole.

modern.text: And after all the nation had been circumcised, they stayed there in the camp until they were healed.

original.text: וַיְהִ֛י כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּ֥מּוּ כָל הַגּ֖וֹי לְהִמּ֑וֹל וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּ֛ם בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה עַ֥ד חֲיוֹתָֽם

verses.restored: YHWH said to Joshua, Today I have rolled away reproach of Egypt from upon you. So name of that place is called Gilgal/Rolling to this day.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Joshua, This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you. Wherefore the name of the place is called Gilgal unto this day.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ הַיּ֗וֹם גַּלּ֛וֹתִי אֶת חֶרְפַּ֥ת מִצְרַ֖יִם מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֞א שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ גִּלְגָּ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Children of Israel camped at Gilgal and made Passover on fourteenth day of month in evening, in plains of Jericho.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel encamped in Gilgal, and kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the month at even in the plains of Jericho.

modern.text: On the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, while the Israelites were camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, they kept the Passover.

original.text: וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּגִּלְגָּ֑ל וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֶת הַפֶּ֡סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֥וֹם לַחֹ֛דֶשׁ בָּעֶ֖רֶב בְּעַֽרְב֥וֹת יְרִיחֽוֹ

verses.restored: They ate from produce of land on day after Passover, unleavened bread and roasted grain, on that very day.

familiar.text: And they did eat of the old corn of the land on the morrow after the passover, unleavened cakes, and parched corn in the selfsame day.

modern.text: The day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain from the produce of the land.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אכְל֜וּ מֵעֲב֥וּר הָאָ֛רֶץ מִמָּֽחֳרַ֥ת הַפֶּ֖סַח מַצּ֣וֹת וְקָל֑וּי בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Manna ceased on day after they ate from produce of land, and there was no longer manna for children of Israel; they ate from produce of land of Canaan that year.

familiar.text: And the manna ceased on the morrow after they had eaten of the old corn of the land; neither had the children of Israel manna any more; but they did eat of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.

modern.text: And the day after they had eaten from the produce of the land, the manna ceased. There was no more manna for the Israelites, so that year they began to eat the crops of the land of Canaan. The Commander of the LORD’s Army

original.text: וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֨ת הַמָּ֜ן מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת בְּאָכְלָם֙ מֵעֲב֣וּר הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹא הָ֥יָה ע֛וֹד לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מָ֑ן וַיֹּאכְל֗וּ מִתְּבוּאַת֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִֽיא

verses.restored: It was, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted his eyes and saw, and look, a man standing opposite him with drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went to him and said, Are you for us or for our adversaries?

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand: and Joshua went unto him, and said unto him, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?

modern.text: Now when Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in His hand. Joshua approached Him and asked, “Are You for us or for our enemies?”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְי֣וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ בִּירִיחוֹ֒ וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד לְנֶגְדּ֔וֹ וְחַרְבּ֥וֹ שְׁלוּפָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֵלָיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ הֲלָ֥נוּ אַתָּ֖ה אִם לְצָרֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: He said, No/Neither; but as commander of host of YHWH I have now come. Joshua fell on his face to earth and bowed and said to him, What does my lord speak to his servant?

familiar.text: And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my lord unto his servant?

modern.text: “Neither,” He replied. “I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.” Then Joshua fell facedown in reverence and asked Him, “What does my Lord have to say to His servant?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לֹ֗א כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י שַׂר צְבָֽא יְהוָ֖ה עַתָּ֣ה בָ֑אתִי וַיִּפֹּל֩ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ אֶל פָּנָ֥יו אַ֨רְצָה֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֥ה אֲדֹנִ֖י מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל עַבְדּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Commander of host of YHWH said to Joshua, Remove your sandal from upon your foot, for place where you stand is holy. And Joshua did so.

familiar.text: And the captain of the LORD’s host said unto Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

modern.text: The Commander of the LORD’s army replied, “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שַׂר צְבָ֨א יְהוָ֜ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ שַׁל נַֽעַלְךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔ךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו קֹ֣דֶשׁ ה֑וּא וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ כֵּֽן

translation_notes: The chapter opens from the perspective of terrified local kings, making clear that Israel's miracle is experienced by others as approaching military danger.

Circumcision is performed on the wilderness-born male generation as covenant marking. This ancient communal rite must not authorize nonconsensual genital cutting outside lawful, ethical, and culturally grounded practice.
Recovery is explicitly allowed before further movement, recognizing bodily vulnerability after the procedure.
Gilgal is connected by wordplay to rolling away Egypt's reproach, though the exact meaning of that reproach remains debated.
Passover and cessation of manna mark transition from wilderness dependence to eating produce already growing in inhabited land; the labor and presence of prior inhabitants must not be erased.
The commander's answer to Joshua's partisan question is literally 'No' or may imply 'Neither.' Divine holiness refuses easy reduction to 'our side.'
The holy-ground scene echoes Moses at the burning bush while placing Joshua under, not above, Divine command.
safety_note: Do not use Joshua 5 to justify forced genital modification, conquest triumphalism, erasure of prior inhabitants' labor, or claims that Divine power automatically belongs to one's side. Center recovery, covenant continuity, Passover memory, dependence giving way to responsibility, and the commander's refusal of simplistic partisanship.
